utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Madam, and thank you. Mr. Oric, can you following the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, gentlemen. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in a language that I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You say sit down and good morning to you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, and also good morning to my colleagues of the Defence. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. I'm here together with counsel, Ms. Joanne Richardson, our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink. And later on this session, Ms. Patricia Sellers will also join the team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, I am Vasvija Vidovic, and together with Mr. John Jones we are representing Mr. Naser Oric. And we have our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic, and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts, with us. And good morning to my colleagues from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Vidovic, and good morning to you and your team. Any preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic -- yes. Okay. Madam Vidovic, you may proceed with your examination-in-chief, and sorry for having interrupted you, but we had a problem with this and it's -- I know it's easier if I fix it myself rather than have to wait, considering that we are limited for time. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony yesterday we ended at the photographs, and if you recall in the photographs you recognised four people, Refik Hasanovic, from Mihaljevici; Huso Rizvanovic, the brother of Nuriz [phoen] Rizvanovic, Almaz Demenovic [phoen], and Hasan Almihirovic [phoen] and that's where we stopped.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please give the photographs to the witness again and the list D647.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the list. The title "List of military conscripts" and to the free territory on the 27th of July, 1992, as the 16th Muslim Brigade. Yesterday you were looking at it and now I would like you to look at page 7 in the Bosnian language and --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's page 8, Your Honours, in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This page starts with the name of Hasanovic, Memis [phoen]. The name under the number 29, Refik Hasanovic, son of Fadil, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the person you recognised on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the person you recognised on the photograph as coming with Nurif Rizvanovic on the 8th of August to Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the same person, Refik Hasanovic, son of Fadil.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just a minute because we need to be to follow precisely. Could you put the photo on the ELMO, usher. Usher, could you put the photo on the ELMO and ask the witness to point to the person he recognises as Refik Hasanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the witness is much better at recognising than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Please try to understand that I am not being fussy. Yes, could you point to the person you maintain is or who you recognise as Refik Hasanovic, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's this person here by the name of Refik Hasanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you please now look at page 14 in the Bosnian. You can go ahead -- go forward seven pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English, Your Honours, that's on page 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you look at the photograph with the number 2?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can the photograph please be placed on the ELMO so that the Chamber can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at this name under number 10, Huso Rizvanovic, son of Nurija, and if you can please indicate who that is on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Huso Rizvanovic son of Nurija.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you please tell us where he's from.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's from Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you now look at page 5 in the Bosnian language of the list?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that's also page 5 in the English, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you can look at the name under 9. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is Almaz Demirovic, son of Hamed. Could you now please look at photograph 3.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Almaz Demirovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. And finally, can you please look at page 8 in the Bosnian?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this is on page 10 in the English, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at person next to the number 7, that is Hasan Ibrahimovic, son of Ibrahim.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ibrahimovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Ibrahimovic, I apologise. Please look at the photograph and point out who that is.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Hasan Ibrahimovic from Krasno Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All these people you pointed out, were they with Nurif Rizvanovic on the 8th of August?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were there Cizmici on the 8th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Could you please keep this document with you for the time being. We don't need the photographs but we will be needing the list a little bit later. Could you please describe or tell to the Trial Chamber what kind of weapons Nurif's fighters had whom you said you saw on the 8th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had automatic weapons, Kalashnikovs, Zoljas, hand-held launchers, and they also had a PAM.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. You said that Nurif came to Ejub Golic and that you attended that conversation. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what Nurif Rizvanovic told Ejub Golic on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. He said that in the village of Lolici that the people of the village of Lolici heard loud artillery fire and that they informed him about it and that he immediately went towards us, towards Siljkovici. He had two groups, one group went to Siljkovici and the other group went towards Djermani.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did he tell you what was happening there, was there a fight between his groups and the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was some fierce fighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any casualties in the fighting?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they said that they did have casualties.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he say how the fighting was conducted, were the Serbs shooting at them?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The artillery was at Siljkovici. There was a lot of artillery at Siljkovici and they had casualties there. There was also fighting in Djermani at Stara Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what did he say? How did this fighting end?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that they did not manage to capture Siljkovici, that they set off in the direction of Djermani in order to get to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why didn't they capture Siljkovici? Did he say?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a lot of artillery there, a lot of Serb artillery, so they were not able to capture it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you -- are you familiar with the old part of Jezestica, did you go there before the war?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what the houses are made of in Stara Jezestica and Djermani?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: The houses were built of stone -- of wood and special material called crpici [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether you found out if Nurif's fighters used PAMs and Zoljas in the fighting?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said that they used it, PAMs, Zoljas; also hand-held launchers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like the witness to look at a new document by the Defence. It's a document by the Federal Ministry of Defence from the military centre in Tuzla, military post in Tuzla, and it's sent at my request. It's entitled "certificate." Your Honours, we have just one correction to this question. To my question: What is the material that the houses in old Jezestica were made, the witness replies: From wood and crpici and here it says "stone."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please try to explain what crpici is, is that stone? What exactly is that material?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: We used the term "crpici" in order to describe material like earth or clay or soil. It was a mixture of straw and soil, and then this would be placed on top of the timber.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's not stone; it's not a hard material?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you now please look at this certificate that you received. It states -- it confirms that Nedzad Civic son of Resid, born in 1967 in the place of Suha, municipality Bratunac is kept on file at the military unit and he was killed as a member of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the place Siljkovici in combat as the a member of the 16th Muslim East Bosnian Brigade. Could you tell me whether you heard of this person?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where did this soldier die? Where was he killed, what does it say?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: This soldier was killed in Siljkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document please be given an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Ms. Vidovic. What's the next number, 80 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D802, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document which doesn't seem to have a number because this is a document procured directly by lead counsel from the Bosnian authority. This document consisting of two pages, one in the original B/C/S and the other one the equivalent corresponding translation into English being received, marked as Defence D802.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look again at the military conscripts again sent to the free territory of the 16th Muslim Brigade; this is document D647. Do you have that in front of you? Could you please look at page 4 of the list. It starts with the name of Mustafa Dervisevic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is on page 5 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, could you please at the bottom of the page, number 3, the fifth name from the bottom, Nedzad, Civic, son of Resid from Suha?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the person, Nedzad Civic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the person you heard was killed in Siljkovici?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't need this document anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, before I continue regarding Nurif Rizvanovic, I just wanted to briefly ask you something that I already asked you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the witness be given Defence Exhibit 176 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, it's an excerpt from a book by Cak Suditic [phoen]. If you can turn to page 2 right away, you can look at this page with the photograph, please. Yesterday on several occasions you described the sweeping or the cleansing. You remember the two documents, one from the 27th of July, 1992, and the other from the 4th of August, 1992, where the word "cleansing" or "sweeping" Glogova was mentioned. You said that the Serbs attacked you frontally, that they were deployed in lines. This is a photograph from a different area. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what you were describing, Serbs being deployed in lines. Did that look like this, the way it is in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's exactly how it looked, just as it is on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can remove the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to go back again to the conversation with Nurif Rizvanovic. Please, do you -- do you remember if Nurif Rizvanovic talked to Mr. Golic and other people about when he arrived to the Konjevic Polje region and why. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. On that occasion he said that he came a couple of days before that in the Konjevic Polje area and that he had come to help us, the people from Glogovac [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he say if he knew that Glogova was in a difficult situation?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said that Glogova was in a difficult situation and he also said that he heard from the people who were deported on the 9th of May to the Tuzla and Kladanj area, which we didn't know until then where these people were who had been deported.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you heard from Nurif Rizvanovic for the first time Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that the deported people from Glogova were actually in Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the first time that we found out about those people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did he mention at the time that he was under somebody's command in that area?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't mention anything. He didn't mention anything about a command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on the conversation with him, did you actually form an impression about where his command was?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: My impression was that his command was in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did Nurif stay with you to fight in the area of Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't stay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did some of his men stay, a small group or not?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a small group of about 20 men stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who were those people?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were people from Glogova, Suha, Hranca.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we now look at an excerpt from a video. It's P328, an excerpt from Naser Oric's interview, and it's tape 2488-6. And we will be looking at the piece of tape from -- on the counter 1.22.46 to 1.24.21.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please listen carefully to what is being said here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I think -- if I heard you well you said 1.22.46 to 1.22.51, but what I see here is 1.23.38 already. I don't mean to interrupt you, but either you or I, one of us is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think I said 1.23.33, but it's possible that I made a mistake. But actually, it is what we are seeing here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please take the tape back, reverse to 1.33 [as interpreted] so that it can be a little bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: ... he sent a courier to Senad Goluvovic -- that's S-e-n-a-d G-o-l-u-v-o-v-i-c. "Naser ORIC: [Interpretation] He had replaced Mircet, who had left to become the head of military police. He had the troops who had been in Pale. He said that he was going to attack Jezestica, and as many soldiers as he had, he should also send to attack, that Nurif had fallen into an ambush, and they had to attack this -- these lines above. "And given that these -- it wasn't very far away, it was close, they got there very soon, after that about an hour and a half or two hours, where Ejub had carried out a very strong attack in the area of Jezestica, and where Nurif in the same way attacked Siljkovici. But he wasn't able to take the whole hill, because the top of the hill was very exposed. They got about halfway up and then they had to withdraw. And they had to withdraw back towards Konjevic Polje. "But Ejub Golic, together with the help of Senad Goluvovic and his fighters, succeeded in taking the line of Jezestica, carry out a lightning action and then return. In other words, what they do is they collect the arms and ammunition and then go back to where they were. There wasn't -- there was no point in keeping that line, holding that line. "Stephen TEDDER: Sorry, how long is this story going to go on for [indiscernible]? "Naser ORIC: [Interpretation] That's the end of the story. I just want to say this was happening on the same day that I took Zalazje. After that, Nurif again tried to break through, and succeeded in coming with his troops. "And then these troops were deployed according to the places where they lived. Some went to -- on the lines at Likara, some stayed with Ejub Golic. And Nurif Rizvanovic, seeing that -- how things were in the town itself, so there was nothing there, returned to Konjevic Polje, and from Konjevic Polje went to Kamenica, and then from Kamenica the Chetnik offensive started. We'll talk about that later. We'll talk about the arrest of Nurif and Glodansko Brdo and so on. "Stephen TEDDER: Again, sir, if I can get it right, tomorrow we're doing the attack on Siljkovici and Jezestica? "Naser ORIC: [Interpretation] No, no, that's it. We're finished with that. No, I won't talk about this because I wasn't there, and I can't tell you any more than I have because I wasn't there. And I'll only tell you in detail about the battles that I took part in. "These actions where I didn't take part, that other people carried out, I don't know the details."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, concerning this part of the interview, I wanted to ask you the following. Up until the 8th of August, 1992, did you ever before that time hear of Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Ejub Golic used to mention him in whatever context up until then?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your knowledge, did Naser Oric have anything to do with these attacks with what was happening in Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to notice that in this part of the interview, Naser Oric said he wouldn't discuss the attacks on Siljkovici and Jezestica because he wasn't familiar with the details?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this part of the interview he said the following: "Ejub Golic with Senad Golub's assistance and that of his fighters managed to occupy the lines in Jezestica. They carried out a swift intervention and then they turned back." You said that in this action you were together with Ejub Golic up to Hrastik. That's what you said yesterday. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, good morning, sorry to interrupt. However, I would lodge an objection to the manner in which Defence counsel characterised what Mr. Oric said about his knowledge about the attacks in Jezestica. I believe what we all heard, unless I'm mistaken, is that he said he wasn't there but -- not that he was not familiar with the details. And Madam Vidovic has characterised it as Oric saying that he wouldn't discuss the attacks on Siljkovici and Jezestica because he wasn't familiar with the details. I think there's a difference between being familiar with the details and being not present, and he said he was not present, not that he was not familiar with the details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is a difference.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: It may not be a big deal, but I want to -- I just don't want mischaracterisation of what's being said there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's precisely what he said, Your Honour, we can read the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Very definitely there is a difference, but I don't know what he said. I mean, we can go back. I wasn't paying attention to that particular detail, obviously, I mean I was looking at the -- following the substance.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's plain as day in the transcript. It's line 13 -- sorry, page 13, lines 10 to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I want to follow you better like this. Page 13, line?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: 10 to 14. He says: "I'll only tell you in detail about the battles I took part in. These actions where I didn't take part, where other people carried out, I don't know the details." So he didn't simply say he wasn't there. He said precisely, "I don't know the details." So I really don't understand what that objection is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If that is the case, that's what I see in the transcript. I think Mr. Jones is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's fine. If he's pointed that that's what was said but, nonetheless, in the interview itself, and I don't want to make a submission, there is a discussion of some of the details. But he has pointed out that he wasn't there, so I can withdraw the objection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. All right. Let's proceed. Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I apologise. I will repeat the question. You said that in this particular action together with Mr. Golic reached Hrastik, that's what you said in your testimony yesterday. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Hence my question is the following: Is it correct that Mr. Golic and his group, together with Senad Golub, captured parts of Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know this person, Senad Golub?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him in that area at any given time until the end of 1992, this Senad Golub, or did you hear of that person?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear of that person and I didn't see it -- see that person there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your knowledge, did that person from Pale as well as any people who may have come from Pale, did they participate in any way in this action?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, otherwise I would have heard that there were there or I would have seen them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you tell the Chamber who indeed captured the lines in Stara Jezestica and Djermani?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those lines were captured by Nurif Rizvanovic. He had a well-armed group or a unit - I don't know what their name was - and we stood no chance. We were poorly armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this part of Naser Oric's interview describe the exact events as concerns Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to that, I wanted to ask you the following, if you remember. Did the people from Suceska participate in the fighting to capture Jezestica on the 8th of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell the Chamber how far is Suceska from this area and from Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Suceska is about 30 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to that I have an additional question. Did Ejub Golic's group ever belong to the Potocari group, ever?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were the Cizmici people, the armed people, ever a part of the armed group from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where did they belong then, to which group, these armed people from Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were with Ejub Golic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to put P95 in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is an alleged document from the 8th Operational Group command dated the 7 of March, 1994. The title is "forwarding of the supplement of the RBiH chronicle guide." Can we look at page 13 in Bosnian and page 10 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to draw the attention of the Chamber to the fact that this document mentions the alleged activities of the brigade with its headquarters in Suceska, 285th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 281st Brigade. Could the counsel please repeat the question, the interpreters didn't find that part in the text.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To repeat then. I asked the witness to look at the fifth line from the top where it states: "On the 8th of April [as interpreted] of 1992, the unit took part in the wider combat operation in the region of Jezestica." The 8th of August, not the 8th of April. Perhaps that could be corrected for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your knowledge, to reiterate that concerning this document, in your knowledge did the Suceska group participate in the activities of the 8th of August, 1992, in the area of Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The contents of this document pertaining to the participation of the Suceska men in the combat, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We mentioned Potocari a minute ago. In your knowledge, did the groups from Potocari participate in the combat activities of the 8th of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell the Chamber how far Potocari is from you, from that area.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Potocari is about 10 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did people from Osmace on the 8th of August participate in the combat activities around Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber, please, how far Osmace is from the area where you were in Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Osmace is about 50 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we can now remove the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Judge Eser has a question about the distance of Osmace from where they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: With regard to the distance of Osmace, if I take a look at the map, I have the impression that Suceska is farther away from the area you talked about, farther away from Osmace and with regard to Suceska I think you told us that it was 30 kilometres and with regard to Osmace you told us it would be 50 kilometres. Are you sure that it's really 50 kilometres? Is it like the crow flies or -- I really have some problems with your -- the distance you gave. Was it 50 or 15?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Maybe Your Honour is looking at a different map. The map we have Suceska appears. Osmace is not actually on D793. It's off the map. I don't know which -- on which it appears to be -- Osmace appears to be closer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I'm judging from my memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I think that Suceska is east of -- no, west of Srebrenica isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You can ask the witness to find Suceska on the map and he'll probably find -- and then ask him to find Osmace, and I think that might solve the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The map, D793, please. Does it show on D793 Osmace or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: It does not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But it has to be there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you find Suceska on the map and show it to us, please?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said Suceska, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Suceska. Perhaps you should look for Srebrenica first and then go to the left. To the left of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates] Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Could you see Osmace? Are they in that area or someplace else? Can you see Osmace?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would say I think essentially we shouldn't -- I don't think we should lose more time on this. I think even remembering where Osmace is, and it's not on this map, I think it is further away from -- from the area where the witness and the rest were than Suceska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I think it is indeed farther away than Suceska, but where the distance is 20 kilometres, it doesn't matter so much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just by way of understanding, when I inquire of some distance from the witness, then I had in mind his area where he was, that is Glogova and Jezestica and not looking from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I understood.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you discuss distances, you meant -- you understood that I was asking the distance from the area where you were?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To move to a different topic. After the events of the 8th of August, 1992, did you, the Muslims, manage to return to the area of Velika Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We managed to introduce a group, a somewhat larger group of people, as well as a group of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you do that?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, Cizmici is a small village and there was not enough room for so many people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it easier to find food in the area of Velika Glogova or perhaps something else?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was easier to find food.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did a group of armed people leave with the civilians to Velika Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A group of armed men left with them, and the group was headed by Zulfo Comic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you after the 8th of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where were Ejub Golic after the 8th of August, 1992, with his men?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in Cizmici, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell the Chamber how many civilians were there with you at that time in Cizmici, since you said a portion of them left.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were about 1.000 civilians in Cizmici at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the 8th of August, 1992, that is during that summer and the fall of 1992, did the Serb forces pressure increase in the area of Glogova and Cizmici, at least the part that you held in your hands?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were daily shellings as well as infantry attacks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell the Chamber the direction of those attacks.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: The attacks were from the direction of Kravica and Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher -- no, instead we will run a video recording. It is a part of P317. Your Honour, if we could for a moment move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into private session for a while, please. Thank you. One moment. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those of us who were armed as well as other people, we ate -- perhaps I should explain. We ate something called djibra, that's ground apples and then you squeeze the water out and you make some sort of a jam out of it and djibra is what is left. It is dried and then we used to feed the cattle with that. So we reverted to that food. We ate pumpkin; we would mix it with corn flour so as to increase the amount. We ate oats and we also dug into snow looking for frozen apples.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Those people who suffered such cold, did they have any warm clothing?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They didn't have any. It was catastrophic. They would mend or patch up a pair of pants for ten times. They used hides, whatever they could find to make clothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On top of the conditions you described, was there a further aggravating factor there?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the daily shellings and the infantry attacks by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And your men, did they try to move in order to look for food and did anything happen to them when they did this?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. People simply didn't have anything to eat. They would go, as they say, just like that down to the very lines where they were captured and killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the usher to show the witness a new document by the Bratunac Brigade command dated the 18th of December, 1992, sent to the command of the Drina Corps. It's signed by Commander Lieutenant Colonel Borivoje Tesic. The number of the document is 04361573.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to read a document to you, and it states: "Based on telegrams strictly confidential no. 2-254, dated 18th December, 1992, we hereby inform you that the line of deployment of our forces stretches from the Drina river via tt 177 towards Mount Tosica (tt 330), above Rakovac village, above Podcaus village, Zuti Most, Zagoni (tt 438), Kaolin, Repovac village, along the road towards Kravica; from the far end of Avdagine Njive, behind Bozici village, Mocila, Blazijevici village, Djermani village, Siljkovici village, Doljani village, Krusik village (tt 234), Neradja village, Rusici village, Begici village, Ocenovici village, and NV (tt 445), Trugovi village, and Sopotnik village. "On average, the distance between the enemy and our lines is between 600 and 1.000 metres." Please, my question regarding this is as follows: Were your lines close to Serb lines? This is already the second half of December 1992.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were very close.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know about any of these lines in the second half of December 1992? Could you please describe the ones that you knew about.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew about the lines. From the top of Avdagine Njive behind the village of Bozici, Mocila, Blazevici, and Djermani.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could you please give this document an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This document which consists of two pages ERN 04361573, one in the original B/C/S and the other one, corresponding translation into English, is being tendered and received and marked as Defence Exhibit D803 -- 804, 804.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please. Now you've told us about the lines and you've seen this document. I would like to ask you the following: Did any group of your people that you testified about so far, either armed group or group of people, was it completely encircled at any point in the second half of 1992?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a group, I already said, with Zulfo Comic at its head.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many civilians approximately were in that area with Zulfo Comic, and could you please tell the Trial Chamber where this group was?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were about 500 civilians in that group, and they were -- I've already said where we were before, Velika Glogova, Vladusici, and these woods.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher now please show the witness a new document. It's a document by the command of the Bratunac Brigade from the 21st of December, 1992. It's a regular combat report sent to the Drina Corps command, signed by Commander Lieutenant Colonel Milan Urosevic. The document bears the number 04363051.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to read to you the first part of this document where it states: "Items number 1 and 2: No enemy activities were observed during the day. Our forces, 1st Company of the 4th Infantry Battalion (108 men) was formed. It assumed positions in the region of Glogova where it replaced a visiting company from Banja Luka." Please, my question to you is: Around the 21st of December, 1992, did you know that these Serb forces were brought, the ones that are mentioned, especially these ones from the area of Banja Luka, being brought to the region of Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because we were observing the Bratunac-Glogova-Kravica road. We were in the area of Glogova, and that's where we were monitoring that road from.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document be given an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document, which consists of two pages, one in B/C/S and one corresponding translation into English, ERN 04363051, is being tendered, received, and marked as Defence Exhibit D805.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us just now that at this time there were about 500 civilians in Glogova together with this group of armed people. Please -- and you also confirmed that you knew that these people, these new Serb forces, were brought in. Did you understand or not that these people were now exposed to great danger?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we knew that they were now exposed to considerable danger.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did Mr. Ejub Golic take any steps?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did he do? Could you please tell the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in Cizmici. We saw what was being done. On the road he stood before this group of ours and he said, Should we go to help those people or should they be just killed there? And we decided to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, at that time when you decided to go, what did your civilians look like, the people at that point in time on the 20th of December, 1992? What was that group of a thousand people like who were with you?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were on the brink of being crazy. There were a lot of diseases, a lot of deaths. It was very -- it's very difficult to describe how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did you set off towards Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When did you set out towards Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: We started off for Glogova on the 23rd of December, and it was after midnight. It was between midnight and 1.00 a.m., something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to ask the usher to show the witness a new document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before you see this document, did you clash with the Serbs? And when?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we clashed with them in the early morning hours on the 24th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we are showing the witness a document of the Bratunac Brigade command, dated the 24th of December, 1992. It's a regular combat report sent by the commander Lieutenant Colonel Milan Urosevic to the Drina Corps command and the document bears the number 04363053. I would like to read out to you item 1 where it states: "During the day the enemy was actively engaged in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. operations and attacks in the entire defence zone of the brigade. They were successful on the Hranca village-Glogova village axis entered the village of Glogova." And then the last sentence in paragraph 2 states: "The air force launched strikes by flying three sorties." Please, is it correct on the 24th of December, 1992, you entered your Muslim village where you were born, Glogova.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's true, it's correct that we entered into the Muslim village of Glogova and that we captured the lines which you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it right that on that occasion you were exposed to air strikes?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both artillery fire, there were air strikes, and action by the infantry.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you something. In this fighting against the Serbs, was it your impression that the infantry fighting you had with the Serbs, was it your impression that they were always linked artillery and aircraft action as well?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was always the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if anyone were to claim that those Serb units in the Jezestica and Kravica region had nothing to do with or had any assistance from the Serb army, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that would not be correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document be given a Defence exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Madam Vidovic. It's a document which consists of three pages, first page of which with ERN number 04363053 consists of one page only. The other two being the corresponding translation into English. It's being tendered, received, and marked as Defence Exhibit D806.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Just to clarify for the record with respect to the last question by the Defence counsel of whether or not the Serbs had any assistance. Could we at least have a determined time when this assistance was supposed to be provided. Are we assuming that it's December 22nd, which is the period the witness is referring to, or some other time period? And this is just for clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic, if you wish to have the witness clarify that; otherwise, it will be asked on cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not insisting that you do. I mean, it's up to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will do it gladly, gladly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, I asked you, not Serbs, but I said Serbs from Kravica and Jezestica. Did you have the impression in this fighting that you described so far, particularly the fighting in December 1992 that you testified about from the 23rd of December until early January, let's say until the 7th of January, 1993, did you have the impression that Serb units, which you said came from Jezestica and Kravica, were receiving artillery and air force help?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the usher to show the witness document, a new document. Your Honours, this is a document by the Bratunac Brigade command dated 28th of December, 1992, sent to the Main Staff of the VRS and the Drina Corps command. The document bears the number 04363058.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, could you look at the beginning of the document. I'm going to read a part of the document to you which states: "The enemy: During the day the enemy brought in fresh forces in the sector of Mocila village, Bozici village, Halilovici, and other villages in the sector of Glogova village, and Magasici village. We estimate that there are about 500 soldiers and a much larger number of civilians (about 1.000 women and children) in this sector. They arrived in large numbers in the evening," and please note this in particular. "They arrived in large numbers in the evening, moving freely in columns despite constant fire from our artillery." Please, Witness, in relation to this document I would like to ask you the following: Mocila, Halilovici, Magasici, Glogova, are these villages where Muslims lived before that cleansing that you described before?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Muslims lived in these villages before.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There is a remark here. "We estimate that there are about 500 fighters there." What is this about? How many people were there? Were there fighters, or what is this? What is this about?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were our people from Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "people," what do you mean, men, women?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean men, able-bodied men, those registered as able-bodied men. There were about 500 such men, 400, 500. I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did all of them have weapons?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many of you had weapons?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 100 and 150.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. It's said that there were about 1.000 women and children with you. Are these the civilians that you are talking about all this time?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the civilians that were moving from Cizmici to Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber if it's possible that what it says in this document was really happening, that "the number of civilians is increasing and they're moving freely in columns despite constant fire from our artillery." Could you please explain what was actually happening?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the case that the civilians were exposed to heavy shelling and they were moving in a column. Some of them got killed. A shell would land in the middle of the column and then the others would just walk over the dead. They would just leave them behind in order to continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that they were going so peacefully?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had to do it. There was no other choice, starvation, sickness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the psychological -- the mental state of those people?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can imagine how it was when you're walking over a dead or a wounded person and you cannot help them, you have to continue. You can imagine how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read out to you a part of paragraph 2 in this document where it says: "Our forces: During the day we initiated the operation of blocking and clearing the terrain of the enemy as follows: A unit of the Krajina Battalion operated along the axis of Bratunac-Repovac-Pajici village and by 1600 hours reached the Pajici-Drmna line. The unit did not have any losses but the enemy had a large number of men killed. One company, the 1st Infantry Battalion, PB, reinforced with men from Bratunac and Srebrenica was supposed to attack along the Bandera (tt 682) - Halilovic village axis and began the attack on Halilovici village in the morning." Witness, I would like to ask you the following that on that day you were attacked by units from the Repovac-Pajici-Drmna direction?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, we were attacked.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know about the existence of the Krajina men in that area, in this fighting?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And were you attacked from the direction of Bandera?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were attacked from the direction of Bandera towards the direction of Halilovici, from the direction of Kravica, which was close. Kravica and Halilovici are close.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to quote to you the second section of this paragraph which describes the state in the Kravica Battalion. It states: "The morale in the 3rd Infantry Battalion, PB Kravica, is very low. A large number of soldiers have fled and they were not attacked during the day and but for the police detachment from Bijeljina, 52 soldiers, they would all have fled. The total strength with the police forces is about 352 soldiers. Most soldiers have taken refuge in houses and are holding their positions, thus allowing the enemy to move freely."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's collection, are not holding their positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Thus allowing the enemy to move freely."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that there was this battalion in that area?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we knew that there were a lot of soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about the police from Bijeljina and the Krajina men?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and we also heard about the special police from Bijeljina and we had also heard about the Krajisniks and we also heard about some men from Zenica, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to read another paragraph from this document. It states -- this is the third section from the bottom. "This attitude towards combat can have no reason at all. They have a lot of support from the artillery, KAG and BrAG, and the units which are in the Bratunac territory as well as artillery from Serbia along the Drina valley. Only one of their soldiers was killed in combat in three days and one wounded while about 30 enemy soldiers were killed by the aviation, artillery, and the infantry fire." Please, did you know that the people from Kravica, these formations that you said were from Kravica, had this artillery support cited in this document as KAG and BrAG?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did know about that because they used that artillery against us every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of your testimony you said that you had gone through certain military training before and after the war. Do you know what this KAG and BrAG stand for?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: KAG is corps artillery group and BRAG means brigade artillery group.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you did know that these -- actually, where was this artillery firing from?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Jezestica and Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct what it says in this document, that they had the support also from artillery in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We were also fired at from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know from which areas?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the Nemici [phoen] sector and that's right across the bridge. There is a bridge which crosses from Bratunac into Ljubovija and I think that that area is called Nemici. I'm not sure, but I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It says in this document that the enemy had 30 casualties because of the artillery and air force strikes. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: We actually had a lot more casualties than the number here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document be given an exhibit number, please, and I think that this would be a good time for a break if that is also convenient for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Madam Vidovic. This document consists of three pages, one in B/C/S, two in the corresponding translation into English. ERN is 04363058, and it is being tendered, received, and marked as Defence Exhibit D807. And we will have a -- how are we for time, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] More or less we're sticking to our estimate that we gave yesterday. I think that I will perhaps need another 45 minutes to an hour more, but not more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And how long do you anticipate your cross-examination to last, conceding that we haven't finished the examination-in-chief as yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, based on Ms. Vidovic's assessment of 45 more minutes, certainly the rest of the session and at least one -- one part of the session tomorrow, if not a session and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. I thank you. So we will have a 30-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's continue. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, we discussed the document of the 28th of December, 1992. Concerning that I wanted to ask you the following: After the 28th of December, 1992, that is after the date of the report, did your situation change, meaning the people who held the lines around Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation grew worse.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember exactly the moment when it happened?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was on the 29th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As of the 29th of December onwards, was the situation grave just on that day or did it grow worse from one day to the next?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was increasingly more difficult.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would kindly ask the usher to put a document in front of the witness. This is a Bratunac Brigade command dated 31 December, 1992. The number is 04363060. It is a combat report sent to the Drina Corps command by the Bratunac Brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to read out items 1 and 2. "Until 12.00, we had not come across any strong enemy resistance. Strong enemy forces are located on the road between Kravica and Bratunac in a place called Glogova. Our forces have gained control of the elevation point Ladja 436 and elevation point Kik by the Lomanac river. Up until now the military action is going according to plan. In Bratunac there are 225 fighters. Taking part in the action are 100 fighters of the infantry company, anti-aircraft platoon, PAT, the anti-aircraft gun, 20-millimetre, PRAGA, BOFORS, BROVING and three tanks." Witness, were you attacked by those Serb forces on the 31st of December, 1992, as stated in this report?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they attacked us on the 31st of December and there were thousands of shells that landed in the area where we were and they kept repeating by radio communication: This is your New Year's present.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember the direction of the attacks?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: The directions came from Hranca, Kravica, Jezestica, that is from all directions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you attacked by the artillery mentioned in this document -- or rather, could you explain for the Chamber what is Bofors and what is a Browning?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Browning is an anti-aircraft gun and Bofors is a 20-millimetre gun used for anti-air defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you also remember that a Praga was used?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we assign an exhibit number to this document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic. This document, which consists of two pages, one in B/C/S and the corresponding translation into English, with ERN 04363060, is being tendered and received and marked as Defence Exhibit D808.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to put Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. another document before the witness. This is a Drina Corps command's document dated 4 January 1993. It is a combat report signed by Commander Colonel Miljenko Zivanovic, corps commander, sent to the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska army. The number is 04267246.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I wanted to read out a part of item 1. It reads as follows -- but before that I wanted to draw your attention to where it says "enemy." The second sentence there. It is considered that there are still about 200 armed enemy soldiers in the area of Glogova." And then further down the says: "Our forces. "In the zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade, the units actively perform actions in the Glogova area. On the 3rd of January, 1993, one fighter from the Bratunac Brigade was killed and two fighters were wounded." Witness, does this document reflect the situation in the field in the area of Glogova, and according to your knowledge did the Serb units perform actions in your area on the 3rd and 4th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. They did launch such attacks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we please give an exhibit number to this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic. This document, which consists of one page in the original B/C/S language with ERN 04267246, and two pages being the corresponding translation into English is being received, marked as Defence Exhibit D809.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we now give the witness D798 to the witness, please. It is the list of those killed in Glogova as well as the list of those wounded in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you have already seen this document but I wanted to draw your attention to some other parts of it. Please look at number 12, and the name there, Veljko Nikolic, Priboj, Lopare, the date killed, the 3rd of January, 1993. Please tell the Chamber do you know where Priboj and Lopare is?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Priboj and Lopare is further away. I believe that Priboj is quite distant.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that in Serbia or in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We are discussing the list of those killed in Glogova. Veljko Nikolic, killed on the 3rd of January, 1993. Please go to page 2 now. And take a look at numbers 19 to 21. These are those wounded in Glogova. Take a look at these names. For all three persons it states here that they were from Bijeljina, Nebojsa Kaicimovic, wounded on the 5th of January, 1993, in Glogova; Jovica Kojic, son of Ziko and from Bijeljina, wounded on the 3rd of January, 1993; Dario Mahmutovic from Bijeljina, wounded on the 3rd of January, 1993, in Glogova. Then number 31 [as interpreted] and the person there, Stevo Obackic from Kravica wounded on the 6th of January, 1993, in Glogova. I wanted to ask you the following concerning this. Just a while ago you mentioned that you heard that there were people from Bijeljina in that area. You mentioned a special unit of sorts, a police unit. In your knowledge, can you tell us where those people from Bijeljina were.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people from Bijeljina were in the area of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How come you know that?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew about that because, as I explained several times, that we had our scouts and we were lucky in that. And they obtained such information and then passed them on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we put another document in front of the witness. This is D25. This is a combat report by the Bratunac Brigade command dated the 4th of January, 1993, sent to the Drina Corps command, signed by Lieutenant Colonel Milan Urosevic. The document number is 00675533. I wanted to read out item 2: "Our forces execute activity in the direction, Tatalj village; Maljevo; Vinjista; Kravica; Velika Glogova village; Vladusic village; Petkovici village; and Brezak; Sanici; Saonik, trig point 503 Vinjista." And then the last part of item 2 reads: "Activities continue on January 4, 1993, until the complete occupation of the direction Bratunac-Kravica." Witness, were you attacked from Serbs from the direction of Kravica on that day, as stated in this document.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from Kravica, all of the settlements mentioned are Muslim settlements. Kravica, on the other hand, is a Serb village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did such activities continue, as is stated in the document, on the 4th of January as well?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those activities continued --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Until when?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until January 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. According to your testimony, attacks were continuous and ongoing. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Ejub Golic do anything when the attacks increased at the beginning of 1993?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did he do?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ejub sent his men to all directions to ask for assistance, to Bljeceva, Potocari, Suceska, Pale, in all directions to ask for help.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when was that, approximately?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the 3rd or 4th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to put yet another document in front of the witness. This is a Drina Corps command document dated 6th January, 1993, sent to the Main Staff of the East Bosnian Corps, signed -- that is to the Main Staff of the VRS and to the Eastern Bosnian Corps signed by the Drina Corps commander, Colonel Milenko Zivanovic, number 04292439. I wanted to read out the entire document. "Based on our request approved by you, a special purpose unit commanded by Mauzer was sent to help out and it was not given a deadline to execute its combat task in the zone of responsibility of the 1st Bratunac Brigade. Bearing in mind the overall situation in the zone of responsibility of the said brigade, the unfavourable weather conditions, to execute the task earlier and the New Year's and Christmas holidays, we ask your permission for the special unit to remain in the zone of responsibility of the 1st Bratunac Brigade until the execution of its task, i.e., until the plan to unblock the Kravica-Bratunac road and liberate the area from enemy forces is achieved."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, since you were familiar with the situation in the field, can you tell us what your interpretation would be as to the implementation of this task to de-block the Bratunac-Kravica road. What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a general attack against the Glogova area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that of the existence of a unit commanded by Mauzer and having come to your area?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you learn of that?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: The lines were close, perhaps 3 to 500 metres apart. And they threatened, they said, You will now learn of Mauzer and who he is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we please give an exhibit number to this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic. Thank you. This document which consists of two pages, one in the original B/C/S with ERN 04292439 and the corresponding -- the other corresponding translation into English is being tendered, and received and marked as Defence Exhibit D810.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to distribute at document and give it to the witness. This is a special brigade guard command document, strictly confidential, date 26th April 1993, sent to the Drina Corps command. Number 04336185. It is a combat report for combat activities between 27 December 1992 and 22 April 1993. Signed for Commander Ljubisa Savic, aka Mauzer by Stevo Pejic. I wanted to quote a small portion that is relevant, first a sentence from the second paragraph stating: "After having travelled for six hours around 5.00 p.m. on the 28th of December, 1992, we entered Bratunac." Then I wanted to quote another passage. "After a day of reconnaissance, our first combat task was to force the enemy as far away from the communication line Bratunac-Kravica as far as possible. Because the enemy had in the area of Glogova cut the communication line, our task was to push the enemy back from the left side of the road to Kravica. We managed to do that without greater effort. We took possession of the elevation points Ladja, Kik, and Pajici. In the next few days the direction of our activities is to be Glogova. We will take over Drmna and Tatalj." Witness, is it correct that on the 5th and 6th of January, 1993, you were pushed back looking from -- looking at the left side on the road to Kravica.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you participate in those -- in that fighting?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the consequence of this operation's activities?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: They attacked us and pushed us back from Bratunac to the right side of the road towards Velika Glogova and that area there, Vladusici, Halilovici, and so on and so forth. So from the left side we were pushed to the right and we were completely surrounded in that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So starting with the 5th onwards, we were completely surrounded by the Serb forces, if I understood correctly?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, please give an exhibit number to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Madam Vidovic. This document consists of five pages in the original in Serbian Cyrillic with ERN 04336185 to 04336189, both numbers included, with a corresponding translation into English also of five pages. It is being received and marked as Defence Exhibit D811.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would ask the usher to put D26 in front of the witness. This is a list of wounded on the 5th of January, 1993, as well as list of wounded on the 6th of January, 1993. This document comes from the archives of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please take a look at the list of those wounded on the 5th of January, 1993, first. I'd like to draw your attention to the fact that -- to the units that these people allegedly came from. Nedeljko Njenjic, Krajiski Battalion, wounded in Glogova; Novak Saric, Krajiski Battalion, wounded in Glogova; Nebojsa Kaicimovic, Bijeljina special brigade, wounded in Glogova. Stevan Maksimovic, Bijeljina special brigade; Zoran Stojanac, Glogova special brigade, wounded in Glogova; Rade Petrovic, 1st Battalion, Glogova. It is unclear whether this is the 1st Battalion of Glogova or whether he was wounded in Glogova. And then Nikica Dragicevic, 2nd Battalion in Glogova. Please go to the next page, then. Stevo Obackic, son of Cvijane, 1st Brigade, wounded in Glogova. Slavko Jovanovic, son of Mladjen, 4th Battalion, wounded in Glogova, also on the 6th of January." In your assessment, on the 5th and the 6th of January, 1993, you saw here that various units were mentioned. Did you participate in these events?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I already said so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the number of soldiers in your assessment that attacked you from the Serb lines, if you can guess?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In my estimate there were around 2.000 soldiers.
