utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you attacked from by these people from Bijeljina? When I say "where from," when was the -- I mean what was the direction of your attack of this special brigade, and you mentioned that they were shouting threats?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: They attacked from the area of Kravica, Repovac, Hranca, and along the entire line.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you see any APC movement?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the direction of Bratunac and Kravica to Avdagine Njive.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whose APCs those were, Serbs or Muslim?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were Serb APCs. We never had APCs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What happened on the 7th of January, that is during the night between the 6th and the 7th of January, 1993, in your area? Prior to that, could you tell me the following: Were you still accompanied by those 1.000 civilians?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were all in Glogova, encircled.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did anything take place during that night, the night of the 6th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were shelled until midnight or right after. And the artillery attack was fierce.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. How did you react to that?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: We reacted by deciding, since the 7th of January is Orthodox Christmas, we felt that that was a time when they were weak, that they were drinking, that they were weak then, and we decided to stage a counter-attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that point in time, did you have any other way out or the option of doing anything else or just the option of carrying out a counter-attack?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We didn't have any other alternative. That was the only way out. Either we would all be killed or we would carry out the counter-attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And where did Ejub Golic's group go?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ejub Golic's group went to Brezak from the Brezak direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the Brezak area?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the Brezak area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you in that group?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And how far did you personally get to?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning sometimes between 8.30 and 9.00 I was heavily wounded at Brezak.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And from that point of time onwards, did you take part in the fighting or did you go back? What happened with you?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was taken by some of my comrades, my friends. They took me and transferred me to Cizmici first, and then after that to Srebrenica, to the hospital where I stayed, the Srebrenica hospital, for three weeks. And since the conditions there were terrible and my wound festered, the food was bad, and I returned to Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you did not participate in the continued fighting?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, I would like to ask you the following: Yesterday and today in your testimony you described a series of attacks that came from Jezestica and Kravica. So I would like to ask you a question in relation to that. If anyone were to claim that at that time or until that time and then on the 7th of January, 1992 [as interpreted], there were only village guards in Jezestica and Kravica, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that would not be correct. I already said that people from Bijeljina and Krajina and Zenica and Kravica and Jezestica participated in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The weapons that they had -- first of all, let me ask you: Do you know what village guards are?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Village guards is somebody standing in front of some houses and surveying or monitoring in order to prevent anybody entering the village. That would be village guard.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to what you saw and what you yourself experienced there, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. would those be village guards?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the fighting you saw Serb fighters in that area, both alive and dead. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw people -- I mean, a man who was alive. I think he fired a burst of fire some 20 to 30 metres away from me, and he could have hit me but I had fallen. He was behind some piled timber.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And how were these people dressed? If anyone were to claim that these people were not wearing uniforms, would that be true?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those people were wearing JNA uniforms and camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you something about Mr. Ejub Golic. Did you in the course of January 1993, after you returned to Cizmici after you were wounded, find out about a meeting that he had in Konjevic Polje? Did you or did you not find out about it?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found out about the meeting that he had in Konjevic Polje there with people from Konjevic Polje, and I know that they picked him in that -- at that meeting as the commander of the armed forces in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to what you know, who was part of the Bratunac armed forces from January 1993 onwards?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were people there from Konjevic Polje and Glogova who were a part of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And was there Ejub Golic a member of the Bratunac War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the usher to show the witness a new Defence exhibit. This is a document by the Tuzla canton defence administration. This is from their archive. The document is by the Bratunac municipality republican presidency and it's a certificate -- actually, it's a telegramme, Your Honours, signed by commander of the armed forces Bratunac, Ejub Golic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to read this certificate. It states: "Certificate. "On the basis of which is confirmed that the Presidency of the Bratunac municipality with headquarters in Bljecava made the decision that the child of the killed fighter, Fatmir Imamovic, into a wing of the hospital Gradina in Tuzla. "Explanation: "Imamovic Ibrahim was killed in military action in Glogova. "This certificate is issued on the request of the mother of the sick child who should be operated on in the mentioned hospital." And in this regard I would like to ask you the following: Is it true that the Presidency of the Bratunac municipality in the course of 1993 had its seat and even after demilitarisation had its seat in Bljecava?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, do you know where Mr. Imamovic, Ibrahim, was killed in action in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ibrahim Imamovic was killed in early January. It was probably the 2nd or the 3rd of January when he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this event being described in this document?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember it. The child, I think, was either wounded or it was sick. I can't remember exactly, and it needed medical treatment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please, Madam Registrar, let's redact from line 14 to line 18, and Madam Vidovic can repeat her question. According to what you know, does this document confirm that from January 1993 Ejub Golic was considered the commander of the Bratunac armed forces?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please reply to that question. Did you hear -- I asked you, according to what you know, can you confirm that Mr. Ejub Golic from January 1993 onwards was considered to be the commander of the Bratunac armed forces?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think we already have an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, we don't. We don't have an exhibit number. And this document which consists of two pages, one Serbo-Croat, the other one in English, being the corresponding translation thereof, is being marked as Defence Exhibit D812. Is there a reason why Golic is spelled with L-i-c-h and Ejub and Eljub?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that's because this was Teletyped and there are no diacritics for those letters, the letters "C" and "DJ." But it's probably a mistake. I cannot now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think it is more than anything else. I don't think it's going to change anything. So, D812, and I sign this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown document P164. P164.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to draw your attention to something written in Dutch on this document at the top and the bottom, and I cannot read that to you. It's a document of the subregion armed forces staff, dated 11th of December, 1992. It states: "Order." The document bears the number 037705211. I would like to read to you the following. "Order." Allegedly Naser Oric is the one who signed this document. I'm going to read it to you. "Prepare all members of the armed forces assigned to the Cerska, Kamenica, and Konjevic Polje units who are originally from Glogova, both the armed and unarmed ones, and deploy them in the region of Glogova on 12 December 1992. "Immediately mobilise all able-bodied manpower in the area of Cerska, Kamenica, and Konjevic Polje, and assign them to the armed forces units in these territories." In relation to this document, I would like to ask you the following: You in your testimony explained to us several times that you lived and fought near Ejub Golic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see this document before, before I showed it to you here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'd never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see here that it states here in the signature "commander of the subregion armed forces, Naser Oric." Did you ever hear of the existence and activities of any kind of subregion?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I personally never heard of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Ejub Golic at any point mention the subregion command as his own command?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at item 1 of this document where it says: "Prepare all members of the armed forces assigned to the Cerska, Kamenica, and Konjevic Polje units who are originally from Glogova." First of all, you, who were born in Glogova, did anyone assign you to any kind of unit in that period?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber how these groups were formed.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: The groups were formed because we ourselves organised these groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you something else now. According to what you know, were there people from Glogova in Cerska and Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cerska is -- should I tell you in kilometres?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. How far is it?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cerska is about 30 kilometres away from us, perhaps even more, but let's say 30 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kamenica is 50 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Kamenica is part of the Zvornik region?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of 1992, according to what you know, was any kind of mobilisation carried out in the Glogova area?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was never any mobilisation carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout the whole war?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, throughout the whole war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You from Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So are the contents of this document correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the usher to show witness document P158.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, look at this document. This is an alleged document by the staff of the Srebrenica armed forces. It's number is 01239545, dated the 24th of December, 1992, Srebrenica. And I am now going to read. "Order. "Glogova Independent Battalion shall be formed of conscripts from the Glogova area. "I hereby appoint Ejub Golic commander of the Glogova Independent Battalion. This order is effective immediately and shall be effective until a new order is issued." Please, in the course of December 1992, did Mr. Ejub Golic have an office where his command was located?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you live close to him, in the same house?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of 1992 until the end of 1992, according to what you know, did he receive any kind of written order from anyone?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look at this document. Did you ever see this document before I explained -- before I showed it to you here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never saw this document before.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look. This is an order to form the Independent Glogova Battalion on the 24th of December, 1992, and that Ejub Golic is being appointed commander. Please, what was happening, could you please tell the Trial Chamber again, on the 24th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you. On the 24th of December, 1992, we were waging fierce battles in Glogova. There was heavy fighting with the Serbs in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And after the 9th of May, 1993 [as interpreted], wasn't Ejub Golic right from the beginning the leader and remained the leader of that group of yours in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now I'm going to ask you something. Please, was he before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Judge Brydensholt is pointing out that line 13 it says --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 9th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And that corrects the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to what you know, did Naser Oric before the forming of the 28th Division in 1995 ever name him to any post or function, according to what you know?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he never did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this document correct, please?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To be more precise, does the document have correct contents?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you now please show the witness an alleged document by the Srebrenica armed forces staff. This is a Prosecution document, P204. It's a small document. I am going to read the whole document to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "Order. "Ejub Golic, commander of the unit in Glogova." Do you see, please? Do you know notice here that it's not a battalion anymore, but it's a unit in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "Is ordered here with to make possible to the military police to take over ten machine-guns seized in Kravica. The military police shall use the above weapons for its needs." First of all, please, did you ever see this document before I showed it to you?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to what you know, were you from Glogova asked to give these ten machine-guns to the military police which was seized -- if they were seized in Kravica? Do you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody ever asked for those machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you a question in relation to this. You knew Mr. Ejub Golic very well. Had he received this order to return, what do you think, would he have implemented it?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would not have implemented it because we lost one or two men for each rifle. One, two, or three men were killed before we could capture a single rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to that I would like to ask you: Are the contents of this document correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... objecting that it is a hypothetical question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Very much, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, are the contents of this document correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the usher to show the witness document P203. It's an alleged document by the Srebrenica armed forces staff of the 23rd of January, 1993, sent to Ejub, Glogova. Please look at that "Ejub, Glogova." The document is very short. I am going to read it in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "Send immediately the missiles that are in Kravica that are with you in Srebrenica, together with launchers and all accessory parts." And please, I'm going to ask you: Did you ever hear of any missiles being seized in Kravica and brought to Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of it and -- nor did I see any missiles at any time during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So are the contents of this document correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the usher to show the witness a document. It's a document bearing the name 01837473 and the document comes from the Banja Luka collection. It's Exhibit D437.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you look at this document thoroughly. First look at the heading where it states "Army of Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Srebrenica SB Battalion of the 7th of November, 1994," and then it states: "Plan for a counter-offensive action by the SB Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Battalion." First of all, I'm going to ask you the following: Did you hand over the weapons after the demilitarisation?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We handed over the weapons to the UNPROFOR who came.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you, men from Glogova, did you ever have the name Independent Battalion, Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of 1994, according to what you know, did Mr. Ejub Golic make a plan for counter-offensive actions?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this possible?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't possible because it was a demilitarised zone and the UNPROFOR was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, could you now look at the signature at the end of the document. You knew Ejub Golic well. What I want to ask you is that did you ever see his signature?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this his signature?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can we have the B/C/S version on the ELMO, please, so that we can see it, too? All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, please, could we move into closed session for a moment -- actually, no, to private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the mentioning of the formation of the 28th Division, did you ever - you, men from Glogova - have anything that could be considered a proper military unit equipped, armed, and so on?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are the contents of this document correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you the following: The fighters of Glogova, until 1995 were they ever placed under the Srebrenica command of Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then in the course of 1995, were there any attempts to do this?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such attempts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And how did these attempts end?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: These people of ours from Glogova did not want to accept anyone as their komandir or commandant, commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Except whom?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except Ejub Golic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the usher to show the witness Exhibit -- Defence Exhibit P80.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How -- is it D80.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P80.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it's not a Defence Exhibit, it's a Prosecution Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I apologise, Your Honour, I am a bit tired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic. Any time you want to stop, if you want a break, we'll have a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No need for that. I won't take much more time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at this document. This is an alleged document from the Srebrenica armed forces staff dated 19th September 1993. It says: "Breakdown of the formation structure of Srebrenica armed forces during the past period." Please go to page 5 in B/C/S. I wanted to quote item 3, page 5, where it says: "3rd formation structure." It states here: "As of half of December 1992 until today the following units have been formed as part of the OS Srebrenica." Under item 3 it states: "Glogova Independent Battalion with its seat in Glogova, commander Ejub Golic, from its founding on the 24th of December, 1992, 322 conscripts, five companies." Please take a look at the names of the company commanders. "First Company seat in Glogova, commander Azmir Golic; "Second company, Huso Music;" then "Sadik Omerovic;" and then "Hajro Kadric;" and then "Semsa Salkanovic." Would you agree with me there's no mention of your name in this document although you were mentioned in the previous one?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you yet again, on the 24th of December, 1992, was a battalion formed in Glogova with 322 armed men?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Azmir Golic in your group was any sort of commander?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not a commander of any group let alone a company.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Hajro Kadric was he any sort of a commander?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Semsa Salkanovic?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To ask you the following, you, people of Glogova, before the demilitarisation did you have any sort of record as for the manning strength of your groups?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We never had any records. We didn't even have paper. We didn't have food or clothing, let alone paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to give another document to the witness. This is a Prosecution Exhibit P93. Please go to page 13. Your Honours, in English that is page 9 on top of -- on the top of page 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It says here "an annex to the guide of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina." It states here: "Glogova Independent Battalion, commander of the battalion from the 14th of December, 1992, to 10 January 1994, Ejub Golic. Deputy commander from December 14, 1992, to 27 January, 1994, Redzo Junizovic." Witness, you explained us the meaning of the term "battalion" before, so I won't persist on that. But I wanted to ask you the following: Was Ejub Golic's deputy commander between December 14, 1992, and January 27, 1994, was it Mr. Redzo Junizovic?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why not?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Redzo Junizovic was killed on the 2nd of January or the 3rd of January in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, usher, give another document to the witness. This is an exhibit, D742, list of those killed and missing from Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, go to page that begins with 195.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there are no pages marked on this document, unfortunately, but this page begins with "195."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Number 221 and the name there -- but first I wanted to tell you that the columns here are last name, first name, sex, father's name, date of birth, occupation, and the date of disappearance or death. Number 221 Huso Junuzovic, son of Redzo. The date when he went missing or was killed was the 4th of January, 1993, in Glogova. Is that the person you said was killed on the 2nd or the 3rd of January in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the person.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you the following concerning that. Did you find Huso Junuzovic's body and did you bury it?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the very same day.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the contents of this document, are they correct as when it says that he was Ejub Golic's deputy from December 14, 1992, until January 27, 1994?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may have a clarification for the transcript. It says in the transcript Junuzovic, Huso, son of Redzo, but his name is actually Redzo Junuzovic, son of Huso; so the other way around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please keep this document with you. We will need it some more. I have P93 in mind. To put another question. You said that the contents of this document are not correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of any person from Glogova having received a written commendation from Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard of such a thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever receive a written commendation by Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever receive the award of the Golden Lily?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that -- if you were ever nominated for the award?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of Naser Oric nominating Ejub Golic for the award?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Ejub Golic ever receive the Golden Lily award?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please retain this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would kindly ask the usher to give P458 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please go to page 32.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is page 22 in English. So 32 in Bosnian, 22 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find that part?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the right side it says Meho Comic, son of Saban from Glogova. It says "was led through by Mirza." And then the next item: "Then I went to Sefket Dzozic," [phoen] and then below "I sold my rifle," and then below, "I do not have a rifle at this moment." I wanted to ask you the following: Did you know Meho Comic?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where was he in December 1992, in your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in Cizmici with me and with my group.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was he somebody who fought for his people, a fighter?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was he a good fighter?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was he an honest person?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you -- do you have any information as to the sale of his rifle?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, is the document correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please go to the next page, that is page 31, my apologies. So the page before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, Your Honours, that's page 22.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the same date, the 23rd of December, 1993. "Zulfo Comic, son of Saban, born the 21st of February, 1967, between 19 April 1992, fought at Pale." And he said: "I was there until a month ago." And then under that: "For the past one month I have been in Srebrenica because of accommodation and food and brought with me a rifle AP-74273. The rifle is with my cousin Zulfo Comic on the lines." Did you know Zulfo Comic?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: We attended school together.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the same person you mentioned as heading the large group in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The contents of this document, are they correct that in December 1993 in the -- during the fighting he was in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell the Chamber, did he survive the fighting in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was killed at the beginning, perhaps between the 1st and the 4th of January.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "at the beginning," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of January 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel and witness please pause between question and answer, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will repeat the question. Was he killed in Srebrenica or during the fighting in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zulfo was killed in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In December of 1993, did he spend his time in Srebrenica or was he fighting in Velika Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: December of 1992 and the fighting you described.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that he was in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him in Glogova and we attended school together. I knew him well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said he didn't survive the fighting in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I believe you have D742 in front of you, that was the list of those who went missing and killed in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Page 2 in Bosnian, number 52, and the name there. Zulfo Comic, son of Saban, killed on the 2nd of January, 1993, in Glogova. Is that the Zulfo Comic you testified about and is his father's name Saban?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And he was Meho Comic's brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, just before my colleague finishes, it's slightly belated interpretation issue, but we had to check something in the previous transcripts because it might be important. And it's simply this: When P203 was considered, in Bosnian you have a word, "raketa," which was translated as "missiles" in the transcript, page 59, line 16, and also in the English version. Just so the evidence of the witness can be understood in its entirety, I've previously used the word "rockets" as corresponding to raketa and it's in the testimony of the 12th of September, I think it's pages 7 to 8 or lines 7 to 8. In any event, there's a reference to rockets and in order for this document to be understood in the context of that testimony we would submit that "rockets" is a better translation than "missile." That's simply that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic. Ms. Richardson, do you want to start now or do you want a break now?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have ten minutes before the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: It's up to you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Very well. So we have a 30-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Ms. Richardson will -- for the Prosecution will now start her cross-examination of you, and then we will continue and finish tomorrow. Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. My name is Joanne Richardson. As Your Honour pointed out, I'm a member of the Prosecution. I will be asking you a series of questions, most of which are -- will be to elicit and to explain further some of the testimony that you've already given here before the Tribunal already. I'd first like to start with asking you about your own professional background, and by that I mean I'd like to -- for you to tell us about your -- the years that you spent in the military and if, perhaps, you could begin in May of 1992 up until the time that you were retired. So my first question to you is: Is it correct that the first time that you were actively involved in any type of combat action was in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And I should also ask about your training with the JNA. I believe you served your mandatory service with the JNA. Could you tell us a little bit about what it was that you did for that period of time.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the so-called ABH branch which is nuclear, biological, chemical weapons, and I worked as a decontaminator.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And I take it that part of your training included training on the use of various forms of weaponry?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: You were not trained at all in the use of weapons or taught about the different kinds of weapons that exist in an organised army?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was trained in using some infantry weapons, but we dealt mainly with the chemical weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay. As part of that training as well, other than the aspect of the chemical weapons, were you also trained in surveying the different areas of Bosnia-Herzegovina or wherever it was that you received your training?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The second part of my term, if you have the military term in mind, I attended a training within the anti-sabotage platoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. Let's clarify that for a moment. When you say "the second term," what period of time are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left in March of 1986 to join the former JNA in -- with the branch I mentioned. I underwent the ABH training and the second part included training as part of the anti-sabotage platoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And as part of that platoon, I take it that you were trained on the use of weapons -- and when you say you -- you were trained as part of this anti-sabotage unit, perhaps you can just tell us a little bit about what type of training you received in this unit so it's clear.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, that part where I served my term is a hilly terrain and people would be sent to a certain hill, and then we had to detect them, find where they were, and neutralise the target. Well, of course we didn't use live ammunition but exercise ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And how long did this type of training last?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe around three months.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And after you completed the training -- was that the only type of training you received? When you said the second part, is that -- were you only trained on anti-sabotage activities or were you trained in addition to that?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I explained the first part, the ABH training, and then just before the end of my term I underwent the other part of the training.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you also testified that you became -- you continued in the service of the armed forces following the fall of Srebrenica. Could you tell us prior to the fall of Srebrenica what positions you held.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just an ordinary person.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, were you part of a particular platoon or unit?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was a member of the group I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And after the fall of Srebrenica, what position did you hold in the Federation army?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also a regular soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And did you retire as a regular soldier?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I was wounded and then retired.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And you were never the -- you never headed a company or specialised in any type of military specialisation? Did you specialise in any way?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because this is not clear in my mind. He said he was wounded and then he retired. He's told us already earlier on during the examination-in-chief this morning that on the 7th of January, if I am correct, at about 8.00 to 9.00 in the morning, he was -- the word used in the transcript is "heavily wounded." Is this the only time you were wounded after which you retired? Because you seem to be combining your retirement with the wounds that you sustained, and I think you need to explain this because -- when did you retire, to start with? When did you retire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I retired at the beginning of 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And when you said that you were wounded and then retired, were you wounded between 1992, when you were wounded on the 7th of January, and 1997, when you retired, were you wounded again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I was wounded in January 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can even tell you the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 7th January. You've told us already. But that didn't stop you from joining the Federation army after the fall of Srebrenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I stayed for a brief period, for a year, with that army. And this was in order to receive salary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yeah, I can understand why -- I can imagine, but we needed to clear -- to clarify this. Yes, my apologies to you for having --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I appreciate it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- interrupted you, but I needed clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: During the time you served in the military - when I say "military" I'm talking about the period of time from 1992 to the time that you retired - did you receive any kind of commendation or recognition or award?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson -- Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness said he was in the army, but rather that he belonged to a certain group. He didn't mention any army during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He did -- I'm sorry to disagree with you, Ms. Richardson -- Ms. Vidovic. He did say after the fall of Srebrenica he joined the Federation army as an ordinary soldier. That's how I understood it to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, but she --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then he retired -- obviously in order to be able to get a salary and a pension maybe, and then he retired in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can rephrase -- break --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I take that your question spreads throughout the entire period. Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was precise in my objection. I said "during the war" and that doesn't -- that isn't reflected in the transcript. I said that he never said that he belonged to an army during the war. I wasn't talking about after the war; that was the essence of my objection, and it seems that it was omitted from the transcript. But that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the question has got nothing to do with the war. The question was: "During the time you served in the military - when I say 'military,' I'm talking about the period of time from 1992 to the time that you retired - did you receive any kind of commendation or recognition or award?" So forget about group or not group -- military is even in inverted commas in the transcript. You've made your point and of course that will be taken into consideration, but it's -- the question is clear enough to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: With respect, Your Honour, I think the objection is very clear. The question saying from 1992 onwards when you served in the military implies that this witness served in the military --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but it's not treated like that. I mean, he can understand because he knows what he did and your contention throughout is that his testimony was that he was in a group and not in a platoon or a battalion, as he's stated a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Not in the military.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Anyway, it's -- throughout the period 1992 to 1997, when you retired from the BiH army which you had joined about a year earlier, did you receive any -- please, what are you interested in, Ms. Richardson, commendation, medals, I don't know, honours, or whatever --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Io, Your Honour, that's the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because the case is not going to be decided on how many medals he may or he may not have received. Yes, any commendation or award?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think that question was also put to him before -- in a way limited by Ms. Vidovic. But anyway let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the period that I was in the military. When Srebrenica fell, some units were formed in Zivinice and I joined then for the sake of the salary, otherwise I had no other source of income.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can understand that. I mean, it's -- it's perfectly understandable. Don't worry about it. Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So you stated that you -- you also joined -- you joined in order to get a pension because you were disabled as a result of being injured in December of -- in January of 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He didn't say it; I said it. He said "in order to receive a salary."

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I added in my comments also possibly also to be able to get a pension.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But he never said it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question, having Your Honour clarify the position.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Are you receiving a pension from the army?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And the pension that you're receiving is a result of being a soldier that was wounded?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is disability compensation of sorts because I was wounded. It is about 40 convertible marks in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And the disability compensation that you're receiving, is it a direct result of your being injured in 1993?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I'd like to talk to you about your -- your brothers and I'd like to ask you about --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps we can go into private session at this time just for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go -- I appreciate that, Ms. Richardson. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: You mentioned that in the beginning, in May of 1992, that there were four groups formed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And of these groups, could you tell us if -- well, let's take them group by group. How many men all together made up the four groups?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number of people. I know that there were four groups, but I cannot really specifically tell you how many people were in each group. I know that in the group that I was -- actually, that the group that I was in was the largest group.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And how many people -- how many men were in that group?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's like this: People were killed every day. They were either killed or wounded, and that's how the numbers changed. You never knew exactly if it was a hundred or more or less. People were getting killed looking for weapons and also they were constantly changing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So just to clarify, at any given point in time the group could consist -- one group - let's talk about your group - could consist of a hundred men or more or a hundred men or less. Would that be accurate?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said -- well, I just mentioned an example. The group that was with us, I don't know the exact number because people changed, as I said, every day. Somebody was killed, somebody was wounded, some new people arrived, so we didn't really have any record of how many people there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So if I were to say there were 500 people in one group, would you agree with that number?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay. We're back down to 150. Is that -- does that sound vaguely in the ballpark of how many men would be in a group over a period of time, taken into consideration the wounded and the persons who were killed?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really tell you the exact number. We didn't write it down, we didn't count the people. People would join us. I really cannot tell you exactly how many there were. We simply were not counting those people.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: You mentioned that there were at least 25 rifles in the group in May of 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't mention that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. How many weapons did you have in the group in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that there were about ten pieces of weapons, and there were also some that were home-made, the Kuburas that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: You also stated that a number of the men or the men from your village were hunters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And as hunters, they would own rifles?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that on the 27th they confiscated our weapons, the part of Velika Glogova and Vladusici, but the other one, well, the Serbs took the weapons from us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did they take the majority of weapons from you, from your village in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And as hunters, I take it that the men from -- were you also a hunter, sir?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: What about the other members of your family, your brothers, were they hunters?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of my brothers was a hunter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And I take it, as hunters, the men from your village would be familiar with the terrain, not only the terrain in Glogova but the other villages and the surrounding area?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really couldn't comment on who was familiar with what kind of terrain. They probably knew the terrain around Glogova, but I cannot really say about what they knew about other places. I couldn't say that they were familiar with it or that they were not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What would this hunting be of -- hunting of what? Hunting of birds? Rabbits? Wild boar? What? In that area, what would one hunt for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were wild boars, animals mostly, deer, game.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, because that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Animals, rabbits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. That explains many things when it comes to knowledge of the terrain, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, you also testified that in addition to the groups that your brothers served in, one of which was led by your brother and we know the name so we won't go over that again, but could you tell us whether or not these groups were known by a particular name? The four groups, did they have names how -- the way in which you referred to each other?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: The men from the four groups that you just testified about, where were they from? Were they from Glogova and other areas?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: People were in Glogova from Hranca, Suha, and other places from which they managed to flee to Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did the men from Hranca also tell you that they had to turn over their weapons, that the people in the village turned over their weapons?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: You talked about the fact as well that you were -- I'll rephrase the question. Let's just stick for a moment on your brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And perhaps, Your Honour, we can go into private session for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: This book is entitled "Naser Oric, Srebrenica testifies an accused genocide of Bosniak -- east Bosniaks -- Bosniaks in East Bosnian, Central Drina region April 1992 to September 1992." And I will be reading from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We've got seven minutes left, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you can regulate exactly when --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll probably have--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to stop here. No, we stop, even if you want to go a little bit beyond, this is why I'm telling you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mr. -- Sir, I would like you to look at page 48 of the B/C/S. It is page 25 of the English. And as you're looking at the B/C/S, I want you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 25 of the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: It's in Sanction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I'll be reading from the last paragraph of that section, and Mr. -- Sir, if you would look at the end of page 48, I will be reading from a paragraph that begins: "The worst genocide occurred in Glogova." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just let me find it for a second, please. Page 48, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: It's on 49 I'm just told. I think it's on the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you find it? Did you find it? It's a paragraph --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, it's page 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Oh, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 49 -- is it on page 50?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: If it's on page 50, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, did you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I think Ms. Vidovic does not agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot find it. Please, could the Prosecutor try to tell us exactly what page it's on finally. Is it page 50?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: We're trying to ascertain that as we speak, Madam Vidovic. On the English it's page 25 and on the B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found it, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found it on page 50. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So let's proceed now. Let's go back on the screen to have the English text because that's what we need. U-huh.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I'll be reading towards the end of that paragraph. The sentence I'll be reading from it begins: "Of the 60 people chosen for liquidation." Okay. Now, do you see the name -- let me just try to help you find it, sir. If you see the name Mustafa Rizvanovic, do you see that name towards probably -- let's count the lines. About 12 or 13 lines down. Can you find the name Rizvanovic?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you see the name Talovic or Delic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, let's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because now we have time to read it ourselves. So let's have on Sanction the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we highlight the parts that you need to refer the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the witness will look at the screen instead of the paper that he has in front of him. So could you zoom in that paragraph, please. Okay. And could you now mark -- all right. So towards the end, three lines before the bottom of that page you see at the end Mustafa, and then the next line is Rizvanovic. And then the sentence that Madam Richardson wanted to read from --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- about the 60 chosen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "Tom prilikom." Can you follow me now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I will read from this portion and if you can follow in the B/C/S, I would appreciate it. "Of the 60 people chosen for liquidation that day, Musan Talovic and Seco Delic escaped certain death. The most dramatic moment of that horrible day was that Muharem Ibisevic stepped between his son, Muho, and Mustafa, embraced them, and they bravely faced death together. Later the villagers buried them together in one grave with father's arms still around his sons. Serbs from the neighbouring village" -- well, I'll stop there. Sir, could you tell us, having read that portion of this book if that's broadly accurate, of what occurred, that was told to you?

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mustafa Rizvanovic is a different man. Ibisevic Mustafa again is another man. These are two different persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: (redacted) [Resumed]
utterances.text: And as for this Tosic it says Talovic here, not Tosic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What Ms. Richardson is interested in is about this Muharem Ibisevic and his two children story -- event. And what she wants to know is whether what you have read here is broadly an accurate description of what you yourself had been told by whoever gave you information? If I did not interpret your question correctly, please --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, no, indeed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- then correct me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That is the exact characterisation of my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is this different from what you were told or do you see a resemblance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's different here. It says here "on that occasion about 60 persons were liquidated. The death planned for them was evaded by Musan Talovic and Seco Delic."

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay, let's stop there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think -- yes, yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is what it's about, and I can see that this is something that's confusing the witness because it confused me as well. The translation is different. In the English version it says that -- just one moment -- that all -- 60 people chosen for liquidation that day, some people were killed. In the Bosnian version it says something else. On that occasion, about 60 persons were liquidated, and this is why the witness cannot understand exactly what it's all about. This sentence is also different. "The planned death was evaded by," so this is a little different in the B/C/S and the English. From the beginning of this case, I have been asking the Prosecution to check the translations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can -- I can take a different approach to this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but if the translation of that particular part of the book is not correct, we need to know it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I suggest is that we stop here for today, you check the translation, and you come back to the witness with your question again tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour, excellent suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Otherwise this will be prolonged and we will be here another 15 minutes. All right? Is that agreeable to you?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, most agreeable, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We are going to stop here. We are going to send you back to your hotel. We will continue and finish tomorrow. In the meantime, between today and tomorrow, you are not to communicate with anyone on the subject matter of your testimony. Of course, you're free to ring up your family but not to discuss these events. All right? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 5th day of October, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
